chapter: New Orleans halls and street bands
title: Crowd words to Tiger Rag and bands meeting in the street
summary: Audience sang 'Jack Carey on the water' during Tiger Rag; bands competed on street corners.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: Well, yeah, the people out in the audience started singing. When we were playing, when we got to that last spot, they said, Jack Carey on the water, selling pork chops, two for a quarter, you know. It just kept on going like that. They made a song, I assume. I couldn't remember it all. All I knew there was a party at the corner of Third Wood at a grocery store. And every time we'd go to the National Park on Monday nights past that, he started singing, Jack Carey, Harry Dog on the water. Jack Carey could sing that thing that's his playing his doing. A parrot, huh? A parrot, yeah. A parrot, yeah.

And it was really good in them days and times. I don't know. Bands meeting up and down the street, get on the corner like that, stay there two, three hours blowing at one another. Here'll come another band, three or four that day. That one play one, this one play one, you play. Oh boy, I was just talking them days. Well, you see those advertising in the halls, you know, different halls that they're going to play? It was like, you know, play at one hall, you're trying to draw the people, I'm trying to draw them, you're trying to draw them. This was one of them things. But it was all good in them days and times. Really good.
